taxonomy.note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO as Ruellia humilis Nutt.

evidence: Hays County — UT Plant Resources Center Purola Preserve lists Ruellia humilis among naturally occurring plants.
Travis County — UT Plant Resources Center's Travis County Acanthaceae specimen index includes Ruellia humilis var. humilis.
Williamson County — UT Plant Resources Center provides a detailed county treatment of Ruellia humilis.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Do not key this only from flower color; use the conspicuous long pilose hairs plus axillary/sessile flower position.

morphology.look_here_first: Look for obvious individual hairs before looking at the flower. Prairie petunia is conspicuously long-pilose on stems, leaves and especially leaf margins, and its flowers are axillary and nearly sessile. That shaggy/ciliate look separates it from finely pubescent R. drummondiana and mostly glabrous terminal-flowered R. ciliatiflora.
diagnostic_traits: perennial several-stemmed herb, often to about 60 cm
four-sided stems with conspicuous long and short pilose hairs
leaf margins entire to low-toothed and often conspicuously long-ciliate
leaf and stem surfaces visibly long-pilose
pale to medium purple funnel-shaped flowers
typical Ruellia capsule with more seeds than the 2–4-seeded R. drummondiana

confusers.separator: Both have axillary nearly sessile purple flowers; R. humilis has conspicuous long hairs/ciliate margins, while R. drummondiana is short-finely pubescent and uniquely has only 2–4 seeds per capsule.
R. ciliatiflora is much less hairy and carries flowers in conspicuous peduncled terminal/upper-axillary cymes.
R. metziae tends toward terminal pedunculate pale/white flowers and lacks the strongly long-pilose prairie-petunia look.

installation_guardrail: May install under the user's standing blanket approval because strict PASS is complete.
